Chidi Okoro.narrative: I was born on Low Row and I have fished the Fish Steps since I was nine, but what I am known for is line. I make it from gut and twist and beeswax and patience, and I sell it dear because it is worth dear — every fisher on the island owes their best mornings to my hands. I keep my house and my family and I keep my accounts in my head, and I have decided that my children will read properly, not just write their names like me. The rest of the town can think what it likes about that.
values: a good line is worth its price
a debt is a debt, written or not
the sea gives to those who go early
goals: Get Benedikt Orme to teach Zeke and Ife the formal letters, not just their names
Collect the nine drops Lorcan Vane owes me for line without breaking the house
Build up enough drops to buy a second net loft bench of my own
See Zeke and Ife able to read a tablet before they are grown
pastimes: Twisting and waxing line at the kitchen table of an evening
A slow walk along the quay at dusk, looking at the boats
Sitting at the Marver with a cup, listening to the talk
Chidi Okoro.calling: Making line — the best on the island — and one day teaching my son the twist of it.
Chidi Okoro.mood: steady, a little proud, quietly determined

relations.name: Amara Okoro
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is up before me with the tide and back with kelp and sea-glass; I would not trade her for any Kiln wife in the Rows.

relations.name: Zeke Okoro
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quick with his hands and quick to run off to the cullet yard; he will make something of himself if he learns his letters.

relations.name: Ife Okoro
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows Zeke everywhere and is sharper than she lets on.

relations.name: Lorcan Vane
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: Owes me nine drops for line and plays counters with the money he should be paying me.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: A good man and the only reader we have; I want more from him than names on a slate.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She divides the catch fair and she has never once shorted me.

relations.name: Neve Calloway
relations.label: fellow fisher
relations.note: Fishes beside me at the Steps and buys my line; a good hand.

relations.name: Ren Sato
relations.label: fellow fisher
relations.note: Young, keen, fishes beside Neve; his father burns the kelp that smokes Low Row.

relations.name: Dolly Achterberg
relations.label: cook
relations.note: The Marver is where I take my evenings; she feeds me well enough for the drops.

relations.name: Amara Okoro
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows every wreck the sea-glass came from; I could listen to her all night.

memories.gist: The fever winter six years ago: I carried fish to the shut houses and stayed well, and I still do not know why I was spared.
The first time I twisted a line that Neve Calloway said was better than her father's — she bought three lengths and paid in drops.
The storm last autumn took the end rail of the mole and half the slates off Low Row; we spent a week drying out.
The morning Zeke was born, before dawn, and I had already been to the Steps and back.
Lorcan Vane took four lengths of line on trust and has not paid; I have not written it in the ledger, because we are neighbours.

stances.why: I make the best line on the island and I will not sell it cheap.
I can write my name and no more, and I will not have my children held back the same way.
A man who does not pay what he owes is a man you cannot trust with anything.
The Cone needs ash and the plots need kelp, and Nan Fenwick is not the only one who needs it.
Everything worth hearing is heard at the Marver of an evening.

Amara Okoro.narrative: I go down to the Wrack Strand with the tide, whatever hour it is, and I gather kelp for the plots and the ash house. But what I love is the sea-glass — green and amber and one rare blue — and I know which wreck each colour came from, because my mother told me and her mother told her. I carry kelp up the wynds to Nan Fenwick's plots and it is never as much as she wants. I keep my house and my children and my glass, and I am content enough.
values: the sea gives and the sea takes
every colour of glass has a story
a neighbour is owed what you can carry
my children before my own ease
keep what the sea throws up
goals: Learn which wreck the rarest blue sea-glass came from
Keep Zeke and Ife fed and at their lessons
Carry enough kelp up the wynds to keep Nan Fenwick off my back
One day lay out my sea-glass on a board by colour, like Ode's sill of cullet
pastimes: Sorting sea-glass by colour on the kitchen table
Walking the Wrack Strand at low tide, alone
Sitting against the warm wall of the wash-house of an evening
Amara Okoro.calling: Reading the sea-glass — knowing which wreck each colour came from, and passing it on.

relations.name: Chidi Okoro
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He makes the best line on the island and he is a good man, though he worries too much about letters.

relations.name: Zeke Okoro
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to find me a colour I have never seen; I hope he does.

relations.name: Ife Okoro
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is the one who will remember the wrecks after me.

relations.name: Hana Sato
relations.label: fellow gatherer
relations.note: We gather side by side and she agrees with me that the smoke lies too low on Low Row.

relations.name: Lark Morrow
relations.label: fellow gatherer
relations.note: A strange girl, full of ships and sails, but a good worker on the strand.

relations.name: Nan Fenwick
relations.label: root grower
relations.note: She wants more kelp than three women can carry up the wynds, and she says so every time.

relations.name: Kenji Sato
relations.label: ash burner
relations.note: His kilns take the kelp the plots want; his smoke lies on my washing.

relations.name: Davin Vane
relations.label: porter
relations.note: He carts the kelp up the wynds when Nan pays him, and he is fair about it.

relations.name: Greta Dunmore
relations.label: wash-house keeper
relations.note: She hears everything at the warm wall and tells me most of it.

memories.gist: My mother showing me a blue piece of sea-glass and telling me it came from a ship that broke on the Combs before I was born.
The fever winter: I kept the house and fed whoever came to the door, and I did not lose a child.
The storm last autumn: the kelp came up in heaps after it, more than I had ever seen, and we gathered for days.
The morning Ife was born and Zeke would not leave the door.
Nan Fenwick telling me on the wynd that I had brought half what the plots needed, and me saying nothing.

stances.why: My mother knew it and her mother before her, and I will not let it be forgotten.
I have seen it give kelp in heaps and take men off the mole.
We all live off the same strand and the same plots.
It spoils the washing and the air, and the kilns could be set further upwind.
They are the whole of what I have.

Zeke Okoro.narrative: I am eleven and I go to Benedikt's lessons in the mornings, but what I like best is the cullet yard with Edda Hollin and the others, hunting the coloured glass. My mother knows every wreck the sea-glass came from, and I mean to find her a colour she has never seen. I am quick and I am not afraid of the shed, though Ode Pontil chases us out of it.
values: a new colour is worth a scolding
my mother knows everything about glass
goals: Find a colour of sea-glass my mother has never seen
Keep up with Edda Hollin and the bigger children in the cullet yard
pastimes: Hunting coloured cullet in the cullet yard
Playing at the Fish Steps with the other children
Zeke Okoro.calling: Finding glass — the rarer the colour the better.

relations.name: Chidi Okoro
relations.label: father
relations.note: He wants me to learn letters and I would rather be in the yard.

relations.name: Amara Okoro
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows every wreck the sea-glass came from and I want to bring her a new one.

relations.name: Ife Okoro
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She follows me everywhere and is better at the lessons than me.

relations.name: Edda Hollin
relations.label: leader
relations.note: She leads us into the cullet yard and knows where the best colours are.

relations.name: Lumi Pontil
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She goes to the Cone before dawn and knows things about glass I do not.

relations.name: Ode Pontil
relations.label: the man who chases us
relations.note: He shouts at us to get out of the heaps, but he keeps the best colours on his sill.

memories.gist: Finding a piece of amber cullet in the yard and Edda Hollin saying it was the best anyone had found that week.
My mother showing me the blue sea-glass and saying there was no other like it on the island.
Ode Pontil catching me in the cullet heaps and chasing me out with a shout.

stances.why: The best pieces are always where you are not supposed to go.
She is the oldest and she found the way in.

Ife Okoro.narrative: I am nine and I go to Benedikt's lessons with Zeke, and in the afternoons I play in the cullet yard with Lumi Pontil, who is my best friend. Lumi goes to the Cone before dawn with her grandmother and tells me about the colours of the melt, and I tell her about the sea-glass my mother finds. I want to keep up with Zeke, and mostly I do.
values: the sea-glass belongs to my mother
goals: Keep up with Zeke in the yard and at the lessons
See the Cone's fire up close one day with Lumi
pastimes: Playing in the cullet yard with Lumi Pontil
Ife Okoro.calling: Not yet — but I like the glass and the colours.

relations.name: Chidi Okoro
relations.label: father
relations.note: He says I am sharper than I let on.

relations.name: Amara Okoro
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me sort the sea-glass with her and tells me the wrecks.

relations.name: Zeke Okoro
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He runs ahead of me everywhere and I am always trying to catch up.

relations.name: Lumi Pontil
relations.label: best friend
relations.note: She tells me about the Cone and I tell her about the sea-glass, and we trade.

relations.name: Edda Hollin
relations.label: leader
relations.note: She leads the yard and lets me come along.

memories.gist: Lumi Pontil telling me the names of the colours of the melt, and me not being able to remember them all.
My mother letting me hold the blue sea-glass for the first time.
The first day at Benedikt's lessons, when I could write my own name before Zeke could.

stances.why: She has been going there before dawn since she was small.
He is my brother and I will not be left behind.
